title: English breakfast in Hamilton, a trip to Europe and pronouncing his name
summary: Continuing the Hamilton story, he talks about wanting to visit London and the pronunciation of DeDroit.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It's an English city. The Barbies wear the high hats and the waiters in the restaurant, they got the striped vest. And he comes up to me and he's bowing all over me like he's a mullard somebody. I'm nobody but he's a top player but anyhow. I said, this is an experience for me, mister. You tell me what to eat. I want an English breakfast. He starts me off with fish. Fish for breakfast. I ate it. I ate anything he gave me. And it wasn't costly. I didn't care what it cost. I make 200 bucks a week and I'm not full of money. But that was an experience that I remember. Because I read a lot of English books. I'm not reading as many now. I go for mystery books mostly. Creasy and all the rest of them. And if I was to go to Europe, which I am contemplating, because my wife and I didn't go when we had the chance. You see when I was 45 I contemplated retiring at 45. I had a bankroll. Doctors took it all away from me. So if I go to England, I just want to stay in London, I want to meet all the jazz musicians, some of whom I know, some I don't. I want to hear them play, maybe play with them. And I've been interviewed by writers from France. I mean take my picture standing around, but they insisted on me in a sports shirt. I do not look good in a sports shirt. I'm not the type. I'm used to being fully clothed, you know. And I'm not that type that's looking for cheap publicity. I hate it, and I'm not the same as the other guy, but that's the way I am, you know. So my daughter said, Daddy, your trousers are too wide. I went down and got some, I'm making a, that was my, I don't even have a hi-fi. That was my combination radio, television and record player. So one of my neighbors, Dell, he fools around with that stuff and I told him if you take it all out, I'll give it to you because I want to keep the cabinet. I'm making a liquor cabinet and I don't drink. But I make, but I put books on the other side. I can't go to my books to the library because I can't bring too much. I'm giving stuff away every day. The other day I parked down on the Burgundy Street. I'm going to say it like New Orleans, Burgundy. Some people say Burgundy. I don't know how to say it sometimes. I have a woman, a colored girl in the library telling me how to pronounce my name. I said, Miss, I know how to pronounce my name. I said, I'm pronouncing it the way they do in New Orleans, which is De-Droit. My name is De-Gro. But I'm known as Johnny Detroit. And I'm not going to correct him. Everybody on the Gulf Coast, they're so sweet. They're high class people. Mr. Detroit, I'm going to say my name is, I went so far to put my name in the phone book twice. I'm going to keep it right. That would cause more arguments. You say, I didn't need to write. Why argue over a thing like that? What a little argument.
I could get you on the phone anyway and hire you.
My idea was don't lose that job.
